en: The app runs on your computer: your data are not sent anywhere.
One or several files, or a zip. In an xlsx every sheet is a table.
Drag over the MFO test on the plot to set both cuts, then adjust them here.
Column of the file for each variable. Time, VO2 and VCO2 are required.
The analyser's columns are read by spiro.
Data read. Go on to Protocol and analysis.
For variable steps, one value per step separated by commas; the last one is repeated (e.g. 300, 180).
Only if the file has no Load column: the load schedule of the protocol.
MRER: lines of 1 - RER and VO₂
Include the resting point in the fit
Read the data first, in the Data tab.
Run the analysis first, in Protocol and analysis.
Move the pointer over the plot to see the nearest step.
The intervals take a few seconds; with a seed they are reproducible.
%s, session %s, added to the group table.
Use codes, not names: letters, digits, _ and - only, up to 20 characters, no spaces or @.
Use the predicted HRmax if none is given or measured
Order: HRmax given here (or in Protocol and analysis), then the peak HR of the graded test, then the predicted HRmax if asked.
Only the groups of Table 1 of Amaro-Gahete et al. (2018). The source does not publish the age or BMI cut-offs.
Compare the zone with the range for obesity
Compute the zones after running the analysis.
No HRmax given, measured or predicted: the zone is given in bpm only.
No range: the source defines more than and less than 35 % body fat, not exactly 35.0 %.
How this test differs from the reference test
HTML report of the current result: curve, results, intervals, SIN, zones and references, alerts, methods paragraph and references. Open it in the browser and print it to PDF if needed.
The group table lives only in this session: download it before closing the app. It can be uploaded again in Reliability.
Two or more sessions per participant (column session) and at least 3 participants; 30 or more are recommended (Koo & Li 2016).
Bias and limits of agreement by pair of sessions
Compute the reliability from the group table.
Both VO₂max and db_graded supplied; VO₂max is used and db_graded ignored.
{n} step(s) with negative fat oxidation (RER > 1.0 artefact).
P2: the vertex (Fatmax {fatmax:%.1f} % VO₂max) lies outside the measured range ({lower:%.1f}-{upper:%.1f}); Fatmax, MFO and their interval are extrapolated.
The {method} fit fell back to {fallback}; no bootstrap interval.
{dropped} of {B} bootstrap replicates fell back to another method and were dropped.
Relative protocol without body mass: the load is kept in W, not W/kg.
The curve is fitted with {n} exercise step(s); at least {min_steps} are recommended. A low RER cut-off or excluding negative values removes steps.
The curve is fitted with {n} non-overlapping ramp window(s); at least {min_steps} are recommended. A low RER cut-off or excluding negative values removes windows.
Fatmax ({fatmax:%.1f} % VO₂max) is at the first exercise step ({step:%.1f} % VO₂max): the maximum is at the edge of the measured range; the test may have started at too high an intensity.
Fatmax ({fatmax:%.1f} % VO₂max) is at the last exercise step ({step:%.1f} % VO₂max): the maximum is at the edge of the measured range; the test may have stopped too early.
No heart-rate data in the MFO test: Fatmax in bpm and in % HRmax are not given. MFO and Fatmax are not affected.
{n} exercise step(s) without heart rate (at {at} % VO₂max): kept in the fit; Fatmax in bpm is interpolated from the steps with heart rate.
P3 model has missing coefficients; P2 is used instead.
P3 model has no real critical points; P2 is used instead.
P3 critical points outside the data range; the step with the highest measured fat oxidation is used.
P2: the fitted parabola has no maximum (curvature ≥ 0); MV is used.
MRER: the product of the (1 − RER) and VO₂ lines has no maximum; MV is used.
MRER: the vertex at {fatmax:%.1f} % VO₂max is outside the measured range ({lower:%.1f}-{upper:%.1f}); MV is used.
The resting measure has fewer records than the stabilisation plus the window; all of it is used.
Not enough resting data after stabilisation; all the data after stabilisation are used.
VO₂max type: age not given, so the heart-rate criterion of VO₂max is not evaluated and VO₂max is labelled from the plateau only. Give the age to evaluate it.
Kcal use the classic energy equivalents (4 kcal/g CHO, 9 kcal/g fat). The default will change to the values of the equation's source in MFO 0.3.0.
RER cut-off ({cutoff:%.2f}): {n} step(s) with RER above it removed.
Last step incomplete ({available} s of {step} s): used, averaging its last {steady} s.
Last step incomplete ({available} s of {step} s): dropped. It holds the {steady}-s steady-state segment; tick "use an incomplete last step" to use it.
Last step incomplete ({available} s of {step} s): dropped. It is shorter than the steady-state segment ({steady} s) and cannot be used.
The Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005) equations cover 40-75 % VO₂max; {n} step(s) outside this range ({at} % VO₂max) use the nearest set, extrapolated.
VO₂max: a {window}-s window is not a multiple of the record ({step_time} s); {n} record(s) = {used} s are used.
The exported RER differs from VCO₂/VO₂ by more than 0.02 in {n} of {total} intervals; RER is recomputed as VCO₂/VO₂.
Cuts rounded to the nearest record boundary ({interval}-s records): {cuts}.
Time read as Excel times (fractions of a day).
VO₂ unit "{unit}" in the units row not recognised; the unit is detected from the values.
VO₂ and VCO₂ unit taken from the units row: {unit}.
An HRmax was given or measured for {n} result(s); it takes precedence over the predicted HRmax.
No HRmax given, measured or predicted: the zone is given in bpm only. Give HRmax, a graded test with heart rate, or the age with a predicted HRmax.
Chávez-Guevara et al. (2023) define more than and less than 35 % body fat; 35.0 % is not covered, so there is no range for {n} result(s).
The range of Chávez-Guevara et al. (2023) is in % of the measured peak heart rate; with a predicted HRmax the comparison is approximate.

No percentile for {n} result(s) with mode "{mode}": the reference (Amaro-Gahete et al. 2018) was measured walking on a treadmill, and the mode of exercise changes MFO and Fatmax. Set the mode in Protocol and analysis if the test was walking or running.
The SIN model needs at least {needed} steps to fit {parameters} parameters; {n} available.
SIN model fitted to {n} steps: the fit is possible but unreliable; at least 6 steps are recommended.
The SIN model did not converge ({error}).
The SIN model converged to a trivial solution (parameters at their initial values or R² < 0). This usually happens with fewer than 6 steps or with fat oxidation that only decreases.
{dropped} of {B} bootstrap replicates of the SIN did not converge and were dropped.
Both a protocol and step durations given; the protocol is used.
{name}: {seconds} s is not a multiple of the record ({step_time} s); {n} record(s) = {used} s are used.
{n} participants: Koo & Li (2016) recommend at least 30 heterogeneous participants and, whenever possible, 3 sessions.
{variable}: {n} participant(s) without a value in every session left out.
{variable}: fewer than 3 complete participants; not analysed.
Differences grow with the mean (Pearson |difference| vs mean, p < 0.05) for: {variables}. Consider CV_log.
